- If sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price history shows mean reversion, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 5–15% for next 3–7 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 10% above recent mean), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at 1.5x recent peak for next 5 days.  
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive (e.g., 0.33 → 1.00), model often lags; add 0.1–0.3 to forecast for next 2–3 days.  
- If forecast mean is consistently below true outcome (e.g., 30d avg forecast < 30d avg true), apply upward bias of 5–10% for next 7 days.  
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.33/1.00), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values.
